newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Chechens blame Russian agents for Red Cross murders.
newsitem.headline: Chechens blame Russian agents for Red Cross murders.

text.p: Chechnya's separatist leadership on Thursday accused mavericks in the Russian security forces of ordering the killings of six Red Cross workers and of local people in a bid to isolate the region and disrupt its elections.

"The structures of the Russian special forces and the Federal Security Service are engaged in financing and preparing terrorist acts on Chechen territory," separatist government spokesman Movladi Udugov told Reuters by telephone.
Six foreign workers of the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) were shot dead at a hospital on Tuesday, prompting the agency and some other humanitarian groups to pull out of Chechnya.
Udugov said Russian forces were also behind the shootings of six people from an ethnically mixed Russian-Chechen family in Grozny on Wednesday.
The Chechen conflict has been punctuated by allegations from both sides and no comment on Udugov's charges was initially available from the Russian Federal Security Service.

Udugov said the Chechen government did not believe the Russian leadership was aware of these activities, which he said were carried out by hired Chechen killers and designed to wreck local elections planned for January 27 and cut the war-ravaged region off from international and Russian aid.
